Reuters links without a paid integration

Passage can discover public Reuters headlines and original links through GDELT. This is limited topic discovery: it does not sync your Reuters account, saved topics or reading history, and it does not retrieve article bodies or bypass publisher access requirements.

If you find a useful article, open Investigate and choose Add a source. Paste its original URL, headline, publisher and an optional note. Passage stores that metadata in this browser; saving the link does not fetch the article. No Reuters purchase or licensed feed is part of this setup.

Optional connections and direct sources

  1. ReliefWeb · optional approval

    The humanitarian-reporting integration is available but requires a provider-approved appname. It can add context about fuel availability, port access and civilian supply. Enabling it is optional; the other sources continue working independently.

    ReliefWeb appname instructions ↗

  2. ACLED · existing account access

    Use the local connection to load the structured conflict records your current account permits. Account access can restrict countries or dates; a successful login does not establish recent or complete maritime coverage. Passage does not purchase an access tier.

    Manage the ACLED connection →

  3. UKMTO · read the direct source

    Automated access returned HTTP 403 in the recorded source review, so Passage provides a direct link instead of presenting an ingested advisory feed. Read the source’s own dates and wording.

    Open UKMTO recent incidents ↗

  4. IMF PortWatch · deferred

    PortWatch is a public reference for passage and port activity. It is not connected to Passage in this build. A future integration would need validated data fields, dates and geographic coverage before its estimates appear in the watch.

    Movement and trade estimates must not be relabeled as observed crude cargo or barrels per day.

    Open public PortWatch →

What this free watch can establish

Passage can help you notice new reporting, inspect official evidence, compare separately dated oil observations and revisit a local reading checkpoint. The watchlist and reporting replay use the records Passage has retained; they do not reconstruct a complete historical picture.

Live cargo volumes, regional terminal loadings, intraday futures, tanker freight and war-risk premiums are not connected. Historical exposure baselines and dated assessments stay labelled. Neither a missing vessel position nor an empty reporting filter establishes that a waterway is quiet, and a price move alone does not establish its cause.

Automatic browser refresh operates while Passage is open. Local watchlists do not send background push notifications. Provider availability and free-access limits can change; Sources shows the actual state of this installation.
